uncertain.note: The print sets 'nevou' tight (no visible gap between 'ne' and 'vou') and there is NO line-end hyphen; transcribed 'ne vou' per §1 word-division normalization (cf. 'conceut in-'). Note that docs/conventions.md §1 gives the illustrative example "qui nevou-" / "loit" for this very line, which conflicts both in spacing and in the hyphen; the page shows no hyphen and p041 begins 'lut', so the word is 'voulut', not 'vouloit'. Reconciler should settle the house rule.

The margin key letter is inked/blotted and at first sight resembles 'ç' (a small mark sits below it, probably an ink speck or offset). Read as 'e' on the evidence of the body marker, which is an unambiguous italic 'e', and of alphabet continuity (p041 restarts at 'a' with ANNOTAT. V).
